listing.name: Atomic Bomberman (Atomic Bomberman — Modern)
listing.summary: A native Atomic Bomberman recreation with its own generated graphics and sound.

presentation.manual_preparation: Start the normal atomic.exe player, not the companion atomic_server.exe dedicated server. No original game files are required for the code-generated free asset set. An OpenGL 3.3 graphics driver is required. Optional original Atomic Bomberman (1997) data and --import-assets preparation remain upstream/player-owned; do not treat an engine install as permission to acquire that content. The normal writable SDL profile for atomic-bomberman-modern/atomic holds options.ini, schemes, anims.lst and imported/generated assets under the current account’s AppData; copies share it and Core does not back it up, migrate or delete it. If preference lookup fails, free assets fall back to free-assets beside the creating player; Core retains this declared local directory, including unknown/custom files during its maintenance. Upstream rewrites its known generated files when the free-assets version changes; its free-assets.txt marker is internal, not a Core completion or save-compatibility certificate. Failed profile lookup disables normal settings persistence and can send editor scheme saves to a drive-root /name.sch path outside the engine. Stop editor saving and repair the profile upstream if that occurs; preserve any actual external outputs. This managed offer requires the normal writable profile, does not sandbox the player and does not claim free-assets captures every fault output. Preserve the whole creating runtime, all effective profiles, custom files and originals before changes. No actual game, editor, import or network behavior is qualified.
